source.quote: E1DA's own page for the PowerDAC V2, read 2026-11-25. « Status: obsolete ». The input line: « Input: USB PCM up to 24b/192kHz », confirmed in prose: « PowerDAC V2 doesn't need drivers to convert stream PCM up to 24/192 from PC/Mac. iOS, Android or Linux ». The OUTPUT line carries the one fixed internal rate on this maker's whole site: « Output: digitally generated PWM 384kHz + passive LC demodulation ». On the absence of a converter chip, verbatim: « You can call it USB DAC + Headphone amplifier(HPA) >600mW@15ohm but actually, PowerDAC has no HPA at all. ... no analog amplification and no feedback are implemented there. » And: « PowerDAC V2 uses the same or similar Ti digital PWM modulator chip TAS5558 ». The FAQ names it again: « TAS5558 Ti 8 channels digital PWM modulator ». The V2.1 revision, in prose only and with no ceiling restated: « Also, PDv2.1 got the new USB audio bridge CT7601 Comtrue, instead of Cmedia which was far from ideal. » DSD IS NOT MENTIONED ANYWHERE.

facts.chip: There is NO digital-to-analogue converter chip. « TAS5558 Ti 8 channels digital PWM modulator », one, feeding « passive LC demodulation » - the conversion is a switching modulator and a passive filter, with « no analog amplification and no feedback ». So `family` and `technology` are both ABSENT: the schema's technology enum offers delta_sigma, r2r, discrete_dsd and fpga, and a fully digital PWM amplifier is none of them. First record in the base of a device that converts without a converter.

_conditions_NON_CONCLUANTES_chez_E1DA: No terms page found, so no prohibition could be checked - NOT the same as finding no prohibition. Measured 2026-11-25: terms, terms-of-use, terms-and-conditions, legal, privacy, privacy-policy, tos, copyright and disclaimer all 404 under /index/; no legal link in any navigation or footer; and a sweep of every page's text for « all rights reserved », « copyright », « reproduc », « redistribut », « terms of use » and « permission » returned nothing. The footer on every page carries two lines: « (c) 2025 E1DA » and « (c) 2126 E1DA Future is here ;) ». robots.txt is Wix boilerplate, permissive, with no Content-Signal and no Claude group.
_lhote_est_bien_celui_du_fabricant_et_il: E1DA's own site is a free Wix site at e1dashz.wixsite.com, and the identification matters because e1da.com is a parked domain for sale, e1da.net is an unrelated Australian IT company, and some twenty other candidates have no DNS. It is the maker's own: the ABOUT US page is written in the first person - « It's me, Ivan Khlyupin, Russian engineer lives in China for 14 years » - and it hosts his own firmware, drivers and Tweak apps. Its BUY page sends buyers to an AliExpress store, so E1DA runs no shop host of its own and there is no shop-scoped terms question to untangle. Nothing here comes from a retailer or a review, although the maker links several.
_un_piege_dextraction_propre_a_Wix: Wix splits running text across inline spans, and a first extraction pass broke words mid-word - « standard un/balanced », « The tut/orial ». The reader re-extracted removing inline tags WITHOUT inserting whitespace and verified against known words. Every figure here is text, not OCR, with no letter missing and nothing restored by hand. Same family as the pdftotext -layout failure met on another maker's manuals today: a silent mangling that leaves plausible output.
_les_courbes_sont_des_images_et_na_pas_e: Every THD, FFT, dynamic-range and frequency-response PLOT in this page's « Tech appendix » is an image. No number was read off any of them; the figures recorded here come from the page's text, and where a plot caption is itself text it is quoted as a caption rather than as a measurement.
_un_debit_interne_FIXE_sur_la_ligne_de_S: « digitally generated PWM 384kHz + passive LC demodulation ». This is the only explicit fixed internal rate anywhere in this harvest, and it is on the OUTPUT line - it is the modulator's switching rate, not a resampling specification for the input. The page says nothing about whether a 24/192 input is resampled to reach it, and nothing about disabling it. So nothing is recorded: reading a switching frequency as an input ceiling, or as evidence of internal resampling, would be two different inventions from one number.
_sept_egaliseurs_parametriques_qui_ne_so: This device is a DSP processor: « 7 parametric EQs », « LPF/HPF and APF for phase alignment and text form Biquad control », « Compressor/Limiter », « Volume slider with classical Fletcher-Munson loudness curves », « Bass/Treble sliders range -12/+12db », « HPtoy App has >30 presets built-in », all controlled over Bluetooth LE. NONE of it is an interpolation or reconstruction filter and none is recorded as one - an equaliser changes the sound deliberately, and a digital filter is part of how the conversion works. No reconstruction filter is named or counted anywhere on this page. A harvester counting filter-shaped menu items would have reported more than forty.
_la_puissance_apparait_deux_fois_avec_de: The specification block says « >320mW@32Ohm » and « >580mW@16Ohm » and warns they were « measured in 24b/44.1k mode +.6dbFS level, typical PC USB2 port powered ». The plot captions say « 374mW 32ohmload, USB power splitter to 5.2V 2A charger » and « 688mW 16ohmload » with the same splitter. Different supply, as the block itself says. And the V2.1 prose says « up to 600mW/channel » against the block's 580. Three figures, all the maker's, none picked - and none recorded, since this catalogue holds no output power.
